question: A 22-year-old woman comes to the physician for gradual worsening of her vision. Her father died at 40 years of age. She is 181 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 69 kg (152 lb); BMI is 21 kg/m2. A standard vision test shows severe myopia. Genetic analysis shows an FBN1 gene mutation on chromosome 15. This patient is at greatest risk of mortality due to which of the following causes?

options.opa: Obstruction of the superior vena cava lumen
options.opb: Increased pressure in the pulmonary arteries
options.ope: Intimal tear of the aortic root

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: FBN1 gene mutation on chromosome 15 -> Marfan syndrome -> aortic root abnormalities -> intimal tear of the aortic root -> mortality due to an intimal tear of the aortic root -> 95%
CHAIN: Severe myopia -> Marfan syndrome -> aortic root abnormalities -> intimal tear of the aortic root -> mortality due to an intimal tear of the aortic root -> 90%
analysis: The patient presents with severe myopia and an FBN1 gene mutation, indicating a diagnosis of Marfan syndrome. Marfan syndrome is associated with aortic root dilation and the risk of aortic dissection, making the patient most at risk for mortality due to an intimal tear of the aortic root.
